assessments.reasoning: The independently reacquired Microsoft catalog names the VBA Language Specification and explicitly describes the defined language as independent of operating system and implementation for conforming implementations. The captured metadata matches the named catalog revision.

challenge.method: Compared the catalog with the distinct technology and VB6 binary hosting descriptions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/visualstudio/visual-basic-6/visual-basic-6-support-policy), the Office VBA7 version terminology (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/concepts/getting-started/64-bit-visual-basic-for-applications-overview), and the separate catalog entries for specification revisions 2.4 and 3.0.
challenge.results: Office and VBA may host VB6 components, and Office releases have branded VBA environments. The catalog establishes a core language whose definition can be identified independently of the host, binary delivery, and edition numbering.

limitations: The catalog statement concerns the core language. It does not guarantee host object models, platform availability, or the identical behavior of any two actual installations.
